data.long_meaning: Derived from the Aramaic name Bar-Talmai, which translates to 'son of Talmai'. In the New Testament, Bartholomew is identified as one of the twelve apostles. He is also known as Nathanael. The name Barthol carries the meaning “Son of Talmai” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Barthol usually hope their child will grow to embody son of talmai and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Barthol total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.
data.cultural_impact: Bartholomew is considered a patron saint in various regions and countries, including Portugal, where he is referred to as "infante do paraíso" ("infant of paradise"); Canada, where he is the patron saint of fur traders; and Taiwan, where he is believed to protect farmers. In popular culture, Bartholomew is often depicted as a strong and fearless figure.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bartholomew is significant as a reminder of the apostle's dedication to spreading the Gospel message. It reflects his willingness to leave his previous life behind and follow Jesus, as evidenced by the name's derivation from 'son of Talmai'. The name also reminds us of the importance of faith, as Bartholomew's identification as one of the twelve apostles signifies his place among the inner circle of Jesus' disciples. Ultimately, the name Bartholomew serves as a reminder of the transformative power of faith and the importance of remains steadfast in one's beliefs.
